candidate_question: What is the minimum order of a connected simple graph having two distinct nonedges whose joint addition strictly increases Kemeny's constant although neither singleton addition strictly increases it?

local_scope_evidence.use: Rules out another broad map/checker build: the retained checker added zero source refutations, and the existing-tool replay only repeated known cases.
Rules out treating canonical graph caching, relabelling, or the prior order-at-most-6 analyzer as a new algorithmic result.

primary_sources.title: A 1-Separation Formula for the Graph Kemeny Constant and Braess Edges
primary_sources.version: arXiv:2108.01061v1, submitted 2021-08-02; journal reference reported by the 2026 paper as J. Math. Chem. 60(1):49-69 (2022)
primary_sources.license_locator: arXiv HTML header, line 27: CC BY 4.0

claim_locators.supports: A Braess edge or set is defined by a strict increase in Kemeny's constant.
The naturally labelled path P7 has the two-edge Braess set {(1,3),(5,7)}, while neither singleton is Braess. This gives an order-7 upper-bound witness for the proposed minimum search.
For a connected simple graph, K(G)=d^T R d/(4m), enabling exact rational evaluation from effective resistances.

primary_sources.boundary: This source supplies the definition and an order-7 example. Searches within its full HTML for 'minimum order' and 'smallest graph' returned no matching statement; that is a within-document observation, not evidence that no minimum result exists elsewhere.

primary_sources.title: Kemeny's constant and Braess cliques in graphs
primary_sources.license_locator: arXiv HTML header, line 28: CC BY 4.0

claim_locators.locator: Abstract and Section 1, HTML lines 35-37 and 48-66 in the PDF text
claim_locators.supports: The later work studies clique-shaped Braess sets and the interaction between individual Braess edges and a jointly added clique.
It records both the transition-spectrum expression for Kemeny's constant and an exact spanning-forest expression.

claim_locators.locator: Remark 5.2, Theorem 5.3, and Section 6, HTML lines 524-570 and 699-702
claim_locators.supports: It constructs Braess K3 examples with no individually Braess edge and calls for further study of changes caused by adding edges or larger cliques.

primary_sources.definition_note: Its introduction writes a non-strict >= comparison for a Braess edge while repeatedly describing an increase. The proposed experiment therefore pins the earlier Definition 4.1 strict-increase convention and retains exact zero differences separately.

claim_locators.locator: Official graph catalogue, Simple graphs table
claim_locators.supports: Connected simple graph counts for orders 2 through 6 are 1, 2, 6, 21, and 112, respectively, for a total of 142 isomorphism classes. The page supplies the corresponding graph files.
The -c option restricts generation to connected graphs and graph6 is the default output.

retrieval_scope.method: Targeted reading of two directly relevant research papers and one official software/data project; no mass scraping.
retrieval_scope.finding: The two inspected papers contain the order-7 example and later clique constructions, but the inspected text did not state a minimum order for a two-nonedge Braess set with non-Braess singletons. This is only a proposal lead.

unsupported_claims: That the minimum-order question is globally open.
That a bounded computation would be publication-novel.
That the order-7 example is minimum before an independently verified complete search.
That the standard enumeration or exact-linear-algebra method is a new algorithm.
Any prevalence, runtime, researcher-time, or practical-impact estimate.
